name: Mississippi Mud Pie Dessert Bars

cookwares.name: electric hand mixer or stand mixer with whisk attachment

ingredients.name: cream-filled chocolate sandwich cookies, such as Oreos
unsalted butter, cut into small pieces

instructions.primary_message: For the Cookie Crust: Adjust oven rack to upper-middle position and preheat oven to 350°F. Lightly coat a 9- by 13-inch metal baking pan with cooking spray. Line bottom and sides of pan with parchment paper, leaving a 2-inch overhang on both long sides; lightly coat parchment with cooking spray.

In a food processor, process chocolate sandwich cookies and salt until finely ground, about 30 seconds. Add melted butter and pulse until crumbs are evenly moistened and begin to clump together. Transfer crumb mixture to prepared pan and distribute evenly over bottom. Using bottom of a dry measuring cup or drinking glass, firmly compress crumbs into a flat, compact layer. Bake until crust is fragrant and just set, 10 to 12 minutes. If crust has puffed in places, immediately press gently back down with bottom of measuring cup or glass. Transfer pan to a wire rack and cool for about 10 minutes.

For the Brownie Layer: While crust cools, in a large microwave-safe bowl, combine chocolate, vegetable oil, and butter. Microwave in 30-second increments, stirring thoroughly each time, until chocolate and butter are completely melted and mixture is smooth, about 1 1/2 minutes. Set chocolate mixture aside to cool slightly, about 10 minutes.

In a separate large bowl, combine eggs, granulated sugar, vanilla, and salt. In a large bowl with an electric hand mixer, or in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a whisk attachment, beat on medium-high speed until mixture is pale, thick, and approximately tripled in volume, 4 to 5 minutes. When beaters are lifted, mixture should fall back into bowl in thick ribbons. Using a flexible spatula, fold one-third of whipped egg mixture into chocolate mixture until just combined. Fold in remaining egg mixture in 2 additions, taking care not to deflate mixture.

Sift flour and cocoa powder over chocolate mixture. Fold gently just until no dry streaks remain. Scrape brownie batter onto warm crust and spread into an even layer with an offset or flexible spatula. Bake until brownie is set around edges and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out with a few moist crumbs attached, 18 to 22 minutes. Transfer pan to a wire rack and cool for 1 hour. Cover and refrigerate until brownie is completely cool, about 1 hour.

For the Chocolate Mousse: After brownie has completely cooled, in a medium metal mixing bowl set over a medium saucepan of simmering water, whisk egg yolks, water, and sugar until combined. Cook over medium-low heat, whisking constantly, until mixture is foamy and registers 145°F, 2 to 3 minutes. Add chocolate and butter and whisk until chocolate is melted and mixture is smooth, about 1 minute. Remove from heat and cool to room temperature, whisking occasionally, about 10 minutes.

In a very large bowl with an electric hand mixer, or in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a whisk attachment, beat cream, confectioners’ sugar, and vanilla on medium-high speed until medium-stiff peaks form, about 5 minutes. Transfer about 4 cups whipped cream to a medium bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate until ready to use. Add one-third of chocolate mixture to remaining whipped cream and fold with a flexible spatula until almost incorporated. Gently fold in remaining chocolate mixture. Immediately spoon chocolate mousse over cooled brownie and spread into an even layer. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate until set, about 1 hour.

Spread reserved whipped cream evenly over chocolate mousse. Cover and refrigerate until set, at least 4 hours. Remove plastic wrap. Run a thin knife along 2 unlined edges of pan, if necessary, to loosen dessert. Using parchment overhang as handles, lift bars from pan and transfer to a cutting board. Cut into squares, garnish with chocolate shavings, and serve.

description: These mud pie dessert bars layer a crisp chocolate cookie crust with fudgy brownie, chocolate mousse, and whipped cream for an impressive make-ahead dessert.
notes:
Optional or for serving: Chocolate shavings, for serving

Make-ahead and storage: For the best texture, refrigerate the assembled mud pie, covered, for up to 1 day before slicing and serving.
Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Laila Ibrahim
